title: Visitor approval at an apartment gate
summary: Let a resident approve a visitor from their phone while a guard waits at a gate with poor signal.
context: Hebbal Homes runs a gate app across 900 apartment complexes. A guard enters a visitor on a shared tablet, the resident gets a prompt, and the gate opens on approval. Deliveries make up most of the traffic, and some complexes see 2,000 entries a day.
Basements and gate cabins often have poor signal. Residents complain when they approve and the guard never sees it, and committees complain when a visitor gets in with no record.
must_handle: A resident's answer reaches the guard within a few seconds on a working connection.
The guard has a way to act when the resident's phone is unreachable.
Two flatmates may answer the same prompt differently.
Every entry leaves a record a committee can read later, even if entered offline.
Residents can pre-approve a known visitor for a time window.
show_in_answer: The journey of one visitor from entry at the gate to the record.
How the prompt reaches the resident, and what the fallback is.
What the guard's tablet can do alone with no network.
